command: dcctl bootstrap
flags: 44

--allow-legacy-db-removal
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: proceed even though this cluster still runs the pre-CloudNativePG event-store StatefulSet (dc-timescaledb-single). 🔴 This ASSERTS THAT YOU HAVE HANDLED THE DATA — it is not a migration, nothing verifies it, and applying with it set destroys that StatefulSet and brings up an empty database on the same hostname. Dump first, or use it deliberately to discard a local instance

--broker-max-connections
  type: int
  default: "0"
  usage: cap the platform broker's simultaneous client connections (nats-server max_connections), devices and platform clients alike. It bounds a connection flood against the MQTT port when that is exposed (--mqtt-exposure): every connection costs a TLS handshake and, for a device, an authentication round trip. Size it above your fleet with headroom for a reconnect storm; devices past it are refused. 0 returns to the server's own limit, which is also what an instance that never set it has. Recorded on the instance and kept by 'dcctl upgrade' when the flag is omitted

--build
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: build images from source into a local registry (developer path; requires source + ko)

--cluster
  type: string
  default: "devicechain"
  usage: local provider: the kind cluster 'dcctl install local' prepared

--dev
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: local-developer preset: --build --host localhost --no-tls --yes, and implies --no-escrow (a zero-config http://localhost/ bring-up); rejects contradictory flags

--dev-allow-egress
  type: stringSlice
  default: "[]"
  repeatable: true
  usage: DEVELOPMENT ONLY, local clusters only (kind, minikube, k3d, docker-desktop, rancher-desktop): let tenant webhooks and connectors reach these private destinations (IP addresses or CIDRs, repeatable or comma-separated), for example a service on your own machine or LAN. Recorded on the instance so every upgrade keeps it, shown by 'dcctl instances', and logged as a warning by every service that uses it. The cloud metadata addresses, loopback, link-local and multicast stay blocked whatever you list. 'none' removes it. Refused on any other cluster

--dry-run
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: print what would happen without applying changes

--enable-area
  type: stringSlice
  default: "[]"
  repeatable: true
  usage: additionally deploy a functional area on TOP of the profile (repeatable, e.g. --enable-area lwm2m-ingest --enable-area sparkplug-ingest). Composes with the cluster's --compact setting; validated against the area catalog (unknown area or unmet hard dependency fails before any cluster spin-up)

--escrow-file
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: where to write the encrypted root-key escrow artifact (default ~/.devicechain/escrow/<instance>-rootkey.escrow). Refuses a path inside ~/.devicechain/instances/<instance>, which 'dcctl destroy' deletes

--escrow-passphrase-file
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: read the escrow passphrase from this file instead of $DCCTL_ESCROW_PASSPHRASE or an interactive prompt (trailing newline stripped)

--help
  shorthand: -h
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  annotation cobra_annotation_flag_set_by_cobra: ["true"]
  usage: help for bootstrap

--host
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: ingress host to expose the instance on (default devicechain.local; use 'localhost' for a local cluster to skip the /etc/hosts edit)

--kube-context
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: build the instance on the cluster this context reaches, prepared with 'dcctl install --kube-context'

--lwm2m-identities
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: path to a JSON file of LwM2M DTLS-PSK credentials to provision: [{identity, psk(base64), tenant, externalId, deviceTypeToken, autoRegister}]. The identities bind each credential to lwm2m-ingest; the pre-shared keys are written by dcctl into a Secret of its own, dci-<instance>-lwm2m-identities, OUTSIDE the Helm release: the release records only the Secret's name and a version stamp, never a key. The identities are kept by every later upgrade, and a run given the file again replaces them and rewrites the Secret (a rotation). Implies --enable-area lwm2m-ingest on a bootstrap (on an upgrade the area must already run). Validated up front (short PSK / missing tenancy fails before any cluster). A bootstrap over an instance that has identities, given none, is refused unless --withdraw-lwm2m-identities is given

--mqtt-device-uplinks
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: let a device publish its own payload to its raw-payload MQTT topic for the decoder on its device type's profile (infrastructure.nats.mqttDeviceUplinks). Off by default; turn it on only after every event-sources and device-management replica runs a release that knows the topic, in an upgrade of its own. =false turns it off; a connected device keeps its grant until it reconnects or its session token expires. Recorded on the instance and kept by upgrade when omitted

--mqtt-exposure
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: how devices OUTSIDE the cluster reach the MQTT broker: gateway (a TLSRoute in Passthrough mode on the instance's Gateway, TCP 8883, routed by SNI; needs 'dcctl install --mqtt-gateway' once for the cluster), loadbalancer (a LoadBalancer Service for 8883 straight to the broker, for a cluster without Gateway API) or none (turns it off). Off by default, so an upgrade never opens a port. The broker terminates TLS itself and plaintext MQTT is never exposed. Needs --mqtt-host. Recorded on the instance and kept by 'dcctl upgrade' when the flag is omitted

--mqtt-fail-closed
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: make a QoS 1 PUBACK from the MQTT gateway mean the platform holds the message (infrastructure.nats.mqttFailClosed). The trade: a QoS 1 publish is REFUSED (no PUBACK, connection closed, the device resends) while the broker's MQTT message store has no leader, instead of being acknowledged and possibly lost, and the ingest ceiling is lower, so size the instance below it. It covers QoS 1 only, and its guarantee is stated for a replicated broker (a cluster installed with --ha). --mqtt-fail-closed=false turns it off again. Fixed configuration, recorded on the instance and kept by 'dcctl upgrade' when the flag is omitted; not giving the flag leaves the platform default

--mqtt-host
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: the DNS name devices dial for --mqtt-exposure (for example mqtt.example.com): the Gateway routes by it and it is added to the broker's certificate. One per instance. Point its DNS at the ingress controller's address (gateway) or the <broker>-mqtt-lb Service's (loadbalancer)

--no-escrow
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: do NOT escrow the secret-store root key. The key then exists only inside the cluster: losing the cluster makes every stored secret permanently unreadable, even from a database backup, because no DeviceChain backup contains etcd. For throwaway instances only; implied by --dev

--no-tls
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: serve plain HTTP instead of a self-signed cert (with --host localhost, a zero-config http://localhost/). On by default on a cluster installed without cert-manager, where --no-tls=false is refused

--object-store
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: where the instance keeps tenant logos and update artifacts: none, filesystem (a volume the chart creates) or s3. Default: a small filesystem store on a cluster dcctl created, none on one it was pointed at with --kube-context. Fixed configuration, recorded on the instance and kept by 'dcctl upgrade'

--object-store-access-mode
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: filesystem store: ReadWriteOnce (default) or ReadWriteMany, which needs a storage class that supports it and is required when more than one pod shares the store

--object-store-s3-bucket
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: s3 store: the bucket (required with --object-store s3)

--object-store-s3-credentials-secret
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: s3 store: <namespace>/<name> of an EXISTING Secret with keys AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, which dcctl copies into the instance's namespace. Never the key itself: no credential is accepted on the command line or written into the instance configuration. Omit to use the pods' own AWS identity, which exists only on a cloud cluster (refused on a cluster dcctl created)

--object-store-s3-endpoint
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: s3 store: the endpoint of an S3-compatible service such as MinIO (an http:// or https:// URL without credentials)

--object-store-s3-path-style
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: s3 store: address the bucket in the URL path, which MinIO and most S3-compatible services need

--object-store-s3-region
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: s3 store: the AWS region (required unless --object-store-s3-endpoint is set)

--object-store-size
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: filesystem store: size of the volume, a Kubernetes quantity (default 5Gi, the chart default)

--object-store-storage-class
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: filesystem store: StorageClass of the volume (default: the cluster's default class)

--profile
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: configuration profile to apply

--registry
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: image registry to deploy from (default: published ghcr.io/devicechain-io, or localhost:5000 with --build)

--restore-root-key
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: disaster recovery: seed the instance's secret-store root key FROM this escrow artifact instead of minting a fresh one, so a rebuilt cluster can read secrets restored from a database backup. Needs the artifact's passphrase

--restore-tsdb-at
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: stop the event store's recovery at this RFC3339 timestamp instead of replaying the whole archive. For the disaster where the data was destroyed correctly — a mistaken delete — so pick a moment strictly before the damage. Needs --restore-tsdb-from

--restore-tsdb-from
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: disaster recovery: recover the EVENT store from this archive path (the serverName inside the backup bucket, e.g. dc-tsdb) instead of initialising an empty database. 🔴 Only takes effect when the cluster is CREATED — recover by destroying the instance and rebuilding it with this set, not by re-running against a live one. When the backups are in the cluster's in-cluster object store, destroy with --keep-backups: a destroy without it deletes the archive this reads

--sharding
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: sharding level for this instance: off, scale. off (the default) is one unsharded event path. scale splits inbound and resolved events into three groups, one per broker server, and is not yet available: it requires the r34 qualification. Chosen once, at install, recorded on the instance and never changed. Leave it out to install a raw shardGroups block from --values (a custom configuration)

--size
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: size preset for this instance: base, compact, perf-12k, perf-16k, perf-20k. base (the default) is the standard sizing; perf-12k and perf-16k are the measured high-throughput shapes (one cluster without --ha, 12,000 and 16,000 events a second with event envelopes on) and need a multi-node cluster; perf-20k targets 20,000 events a second on the same shape with more broker CPU (throughput sizing, latency unvalidated); compact is the cluster's own setting (dcctl install --size compact), accepted here only on a compact cluster. Recorded on the instance and re-applied by every upgrade. A --values overlay, and an OpenTofu variable you state yourself, win over the preset

--skip-preflight
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: skip the local-system preflight checks

--sparkplug-source
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: path to a YAML or JSON file of Sparkplug sources to connect: a list of {tenant, hostId, broker{url, username, password | passwordFile | passwordSecretRef{name, key}}, groups, deviceTypeToken, autoRegister, commands{enabled, hostRole, writableMetrics, ...}}. Each source is one Host Application connection out to a customer broker, bound to one tenant. The broker password is written by dcctl into a Secret of its own, dci-<instance>-sparkplug-broker, OUTSIDE the Helm release: the release records only the Secret's name and a salted digest, never the password (or name a Secret you manage yourself with passwordSecretRef, which dcctl neither reads nor writes). The sources are kept by every later upgrade. Implies --enable-area sparkplug-ingest on a bootstrap (on an upgrade the area must already run). Validated up front. A bootstrap over an instance that has sources, given none, is refused unless --withdraw-sparkplug-sources is given

--trusted-proxies
  type: stringSlice
  default: "[]"
  repeatable: true
  usage: CIDR ranges of the proxies whose X-Forwarded-For the services believe (infrastructure.http.trustedProxies); repeat or comma-separate. Default: the cluster's pod range, read from its nodes, which is where the ingress controller runs; add a fronting load balancer's ranges when there is one. It is recorded on the instance and kept by every upgrade; "auto" returns to deriving it from the cluster

--values
  type: stringArray
  default: "[]"
  repeatable: true
  usage: a YAML file of operator tuning (replica counts, resources, an area's own configuration), merged over the values dcctl computes (repeatable; later files win). The overlay is recorded on the instance, so 'dcctl upgrade' keeps applying it; on upgrade, --values REPLACES the recorded overlay. Only tunable values are accepted: a key dcctl owns (images, credentials, endpoints, ingress host and TLS, the area set) is refused, naming it, before anything changes

--version
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: image version/tag to deploy (default: the published release version, or 'dev' with --build)

--withdraw-lwm2m-identities
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: remove the instance's LwM2M identities and the Secret holding their pre-shared keys. Not combinable with --lwm2m-identities

--withdraw-sparkplug-sources
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: remove the instance's Sparkplug sources and the Secret holding their broker passwords. Not combinable with --sparkplug-source

--yes
  shorthand: -y
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: assume yes for prompts
